records.title: 225xe Plug-in Hybrid High-Voltage Battery Fire Risk (2020 Recall)
records.description: On 225xe plug-in hybrid Active Tourers built in 2020, a manufacturing defect left welding-bead particles and cell contamination inside the high-voltage battery pack. During charging this debris can cause an internal short circuit between modules, which may trigger a thermal chain reaction and a fire. BMW issued a worldwide PHEV recall (initially ~4,500 cars, later expanded to ~26,700 across 11 PHEV models). Affected owners were told NOT to charge the car and to run on the combustion engine only until the pack was inspected/replaced. Separately, 225xe owners report cell imbalance, BMS communication faults, capacity loss and inconsistent charging as the pack ages.
records.solution: Confirm the VIN against the PHEV battery recall (EU Rapex alerts 41/2020 and 49/2020); BMW inspects and replaces affected high-voltage batteries free of charge. For age-related faults, a dealer HV diagnostic identifies the failed cell module; remedy is module/pack replacement.
symptoms: Will not charge / inconsistent charge times

records.title: B38 Three-Cylinder Petrol Timing Chain Stretch / Cold-Start Rattle
records.description: The 1.5-litre three-cylinder B38 petrol engine (216i/218i) can suffer timing-chain elongation. The higher per-cylinder load on a three-pot stresses the chain, and worn chain tensioners lose the ability to keep correct tension. The classic symptom is a metallic rattle for a few seconds on cold start, typically appearing around 80,000-120,000 km, accompanied by rough running and power loss. Neglected oil changes and extreme short-trip driving accelerate the wear. If the stretched chain jumps a tooth the pistons can contact the valves, causing major engine damage. Early B38 manual cars (pre-April 2015) also had isolated crankshaft axial-bearing failures.
records.solution: Replace the timing chain, guides and tensioner as a set at the first sign of cold-start rattle rather than waiting for failure. Prevent recurrence with on-time oil services using BMW Longlife-spec oil and avoiding constant very short journeys.

records.title: Diesel EGR Cooler Glycol Leak Causing Intake Manifold Melt / Fire Risk
records.description: On diesel models the exhaust-gas-recirculation (EGR) cooler can develop internal cracks in its cooling fins, allowing ethylene glycol coolant to leak into the intake tract. There it mixes with carbon soot and, at high exhaust temperatures, this sticky mixture can ignite, melting the plastic intake manifold and in rare cases causing an engine-bay fire. This is part of the wider BMW N47/B47/N57 EGR campaign that grew to roughly 800,000 vehicles worldwide; the 2 Series Active Tourer/Gran Tourer diesel was added to the recall and a second UK recall (R/2023/172) was launched in June 2023 covering build dates Feb 2015 to Mar 2018. Owners also report a second EGR valve failure occurring after the recall cooler is fitted.
records.solution: Have the EGR cooler replaced with the optimised component free of charge under recall (UK recall R/2023/172, BMW ref 0011020700). Check the VIN against BMW/DVSA recall records; if coolant loss, white exhaust smoke or a coolant smell appears, stop driving and book the work immediately.

records.title: Diesel Swirl Flap Sticking / Carbon Build-up Causing Limp Mode
records.description: The intake swirl flaps in the diesel intake manifold are moved by an electric actuator and self-check from open to closed each time the ignition is switched on. Carbon build-up (worsened by EGR soot, common in short-trip and EGR-affected cars) makes the flaps and linkage stick or travel beyond their expected range. The DDE then interprets this as a faulty swirl-flap system and puts the car into limp mode with reduced power. Stuck-closed flaps cost around 10% top-end power; stuck-open hurts low-speed driveability.
records.solution: Read DDE swirl-flap actuator codes, then clean or free the flaps and linkage of carbon, or replace the actuator/intake manifold if worn. Some owners fit swirl-flap delete/blanking plates as a permanent fix with no meaningful performance/economy change. Addressing EGR soot reduces recurrence.

records.title: Electromechanical (EMF) Parking Brake Failure / False Warning
records.description: The electric parking brake can throw a 'Parking brake malfunction' Check Control message on the central display even when the brake is physically applied, and sometimes will not release until the engine is cycled off and on. Two causes are documented: an EMF actuator motor on a rear caliper that was manufactured incorrectly and can fail, and (on 2015-2016 Gran Tourer cars) fault 420106 from a faulty spring in the gear selector sending a false signal to the parking-brake module. Fault codes are stored in the EMF module, not the main ECU, so a BMW-capable scanner is needed to diagnose.
records.solution: Diagnose with BMW-specific equipment (e.g. ISTA) to read the EMF module. Remedy is replacing the failed EMF caliper actuator, or for the false-signal fault, replacing the faulty gear-selector spring/switch. Many cases were covered under warranty.
symptoms: Parking brake will not release until restart

records.title: Front Suspension Strut Top Mount / Creaking & Knocking Over Bumps
records.description: Owners commonly report creaking, clunking or knocking from the front suspension over uneven surfaces and small ridges, often appearing very early (some at 8,000-9,000 miles). The cause is typically the front strut top mount / top bearing, worn foam cushions or spring pads that develop a gap against the strut shaft, plus tie-bar bushes. A fractured front anti-roll bar has also been reported on an early car. The noise is also noticeable when turning the steering at low speed when cold.
records.solution: Inspect strut top mounts/bearings, spring pads and bump-stop cushions and anti-roll bar links; replace the worn top mount(s) and bushes. Many early cars were repaired under warranty. Confirm the noise is not just the bonnet/cowl by isolating components on a lift.
symptoms: Creaking when steering at low speed (esp. cold)

records.title: Spurious Collision Warning / Autonomous Emergency Braking Activation
records.description: Cars fitted with the Driving Assistant collision-warning system have had the forward-collision warning and autonomous emergency braking misbehave: on some 2016 cars the system repeatedly warned/intervened with no obstacle present (dealers replaced brake switches without fully resolving it), and one 2018 owner reported the anti-collision braking spuriously locking all four wheels at ~50 mph. This is a genuine safety concern because an unexpected hard brake application can cause loss of control or a rear-end collision.
records.solution: Have BMW diagnose the camera/radar driving-assistant module and brake-light switch; remedy can involve brake-switch replacement, sensor recalibration or software update. Persistent cases should be escalated to BMW and the national authority (DVSA in the UK) given the safety implications.
symptoms: Wheels locking with no obstacle present
